about.title: About this page
about.html:
How to read it

If a run is red (> 30 h old), the screen is out of date – ask for a refresh.

What you see

  • Short notes on the page's panels (what the colours mean); full notes behind each panel's ⓘ.
  • Forecast runs on screen (NEM time): IFS, AIFS, ensemble run time + hours old (red if > 30 h); seasonal month.
  • Download progress while a refresh runs (W-016): which model, step x of y, %, GB so far.
  • Cloud (W-019): when the cloud last made new data, when Weather last checked, next check (every hour).
  • Reminder: new data only when a refresh is asked for. Data credit: ECMWF, CC BY 4.0.

Limits

Notes are a summary – the full explanation is in the tab's card (S1, M1, C1, L1).

compare.title: Region, AI model vs main model
compare.html:
How to read it

  • Agreement = more confidence. A yellow cell = check M1: is the ensemble range wide on that day too?
  • AIFS is usually smoother: smaller peaks, less extreme rain. A big IFS rain day that AIFS doesn't show is a "maybe".

What you see

  • Title bar: code C1 · region picker (NSW / QLD / VIC / SA / TAS) · field picker (Temperature / Wind 100 m / Solar / Rain) · ⓘ (this card's "How to read it") · ▁ minimise. Edit mode adds A− / A+ (text size) and ✕ (remove). Region and field are remembered per panel, so a page can hold e.g. NSW temperature next to NSW wind.
  • Temperature / Wind 100 m: blue line = IFS, purple line = AIFS, to 15 days.
  • Rain / Solar: daily totals, blue bar = IFS, purple bar = AIFS.
  • Table: each day "IFS / AIFS" for High, Low, Rain, Wind, Sun. Yellow = big difference (≥ 3 °C, ≥ 5 mm rain, ≥ 10 km/h wind, ≥ 1.5 kWh/m² sun).

Limits

  • AIFS has no true hourly max/min: its High/Low are the warmest/coolest 6-hourly values → can look milder.
  • Both are single runs: neither shows uncertainty by itself.

changes.title: What changed between two runs
changes.html:
How to read it

  • Changes in the next 1–3 days matter most – the forecast is firming up. Big changes at day 8–15 are normal (the model is still guessing) – treat them as "watch this".
  • A change in the ensemble middle is more meaningful than a change in a single run (IFS or AIFS), which can jump around from run to run.
  • Compare like with like: today 10:00 vs yesterday 10:00 (the default) avoids small day/night differences between runs.

What you see

  • Title bar: code D1 · model picker (IFS / AIFS (AI) / Ensemble middle) · run picker (default: latest) · vs picker (any earlier run on disk; default: the same time yesterday, else the run before) · ⓘ · ▁.
  • Table, all 5 regions (NSW, QLD, VIC, SA, TAS), only the notable changes, sorted by day: Region · Day · what changed, as "old → new (change)", e.g. High 25 → 28 (+3 °C), Rain chance 20% → 70%.
  • Notable = high or low ±2 °C or more · rain ±5 mm or more · rain chance ±30 points or more (ensemble only) · wind ±10 km/h or more · sun ±1.5 kWh/m² or more. Bigger changes in bold.
  • "No big changes" when nothing passes the limits.

Limits

  • Only runs that were downloaded can be picked (refresh fetches the newest run only).
  • Wind and sun changes use day averages / totals – a change in timing within the day is not shown.

map.title: East-coast map
map.html:
How to read it

  • Temperature: blue cool → red hot. Wind: white calm → purple strong. Solar: dark → yellow bright. Rain: white dry → dark blue heavy.
  • Rain is mm per hour averaged over the step before the time shown (so 3 h / 6 h / 12 h steps compare); solar is the average over that step.
  • Seasonal: blue/brown = below normal, red/green = above normal; white = normal.
  • Colour scale fits the data on screen (except solar 0–1100 W/m² and rain from 0) – compare colours within one map, not between maps.

What you see

  • Title bar: code G1 · model picker (IFS / AIFS (AI) / Ensemble middle / Seasonal) · field picker · ⓘ · ▁. Bottom strip: time (NEM) with ◀ / ▶ and a slider; opens at the next forecast time from now. Model, field are remembered per panel.
  • Run pickers (W-017): run (default: latest; maps are kept 30 days) and vs (– none – or an earlier run).
  • With a vs run = change map: colours show chosen run minus vs run at the same time (temperature: red = warmer now, blue = cooler; rain: green = wetter now, brown = drier; wind / solar likewise). Only times both runs cover; seasonal: same month.
  • Colour map of the east coast (lat −9 to −44, lon 129 to 155): one square per 0.25° (~25 km); seasonal 1°.
  • Black line = coastline (from ECMWF's land/sea mask). Dots = the 5 cities.
  • Colour scale on the right with min / max and unit.

Limits

  • The ensemble map shows the middle run only (no range on the map).
  • Map data is kept 30 days.

insights.title: Insights: what the latest run says and what changed
insights.html:
How to read it

  • Headlines first; open the page's charts for the detail.
  • "Changed since" in the next 1–3 days is the forecast firming up and matters most. Changes at day 8–15 are early signs.
  • The wind rules use the city grid square. They hint at wind-farm weather but are not wind-farm output.

What you see

  • Title bar: code I1 · page picker · ⓘ · ▁. The subtitle shows which runs are compared, e.g. "20 Oct 10:00 vs 19 Oct 10:00".
  • Headlines: up to 5 bullets with the biggest things, most important first. Red = heat / storm-type risk, blue = cold, amber = wind or solar, grey = for information.
  • By region: NSW, QLD, VIC, SA, each a few bullets (e.g. Thu 34 °C – hottest day; dull day Fri (2.1 kWh/m²)).
  • Changed since <earlier run>: the notable changes, e.g. NSW Thu high 31 → 34 °C (+3), SA Sat rain chance 20 → 70 %.
  • "Nothing stands out" when no rule fires.

Limits

  • Rules, not a forecaster: the wording is fixed and simple.
  • TAS is left out on purpose (small position). Ask to add it back.
  • With only one run on disk there's no "Changed since" (it says so).

seasonal.title: Region, 6-month outlook vs normal
seasonal.html:
How to read it

  • Look at the chance, not just the bar: +0.3 °C with 90 % chance is a stronger signal than +0.8 °C with 60 %.
  • ~50 % = no signal. 70 %+ = a clear lean. Both models leaning the same way = more confidence.
  • Month 1 is the current month (part already happened).

What you see

  • Title bar: code L1 · region picker (NSW / QLD / VIC / SA / TAS) · field picker (Temperature / Wind 10 m / Solar / Rain) · ⓘ (this card's "How to read it") · ▁ minimise. Edit mode adds A− / A+ (text size) and ✕ (remove). Region and field are remembered per panel, so a page can hold e.g. NSW temperature next to NSW wind.
  • Run pickers (W-017): forecast month (default: latest) and vs (– none – or any earlier month on disk; default: last month). Remembered per panel.
  • With a vs month: a ◆ marker on each bar = last month's forecast for the same month (ECMWF and BOM); table Change column = change in chance above normal (e.g. 60 → 85 %). Only months both forecasts cover.
  • Bars per month: left = ECMWF SEAS5 (average of 51 runs), right = BOM ACCESS-S2 (average of its runs, lighter colour). Red = above normal, blue = below for temperature; green/brown for rain; orange/purple for wind and solar.
  • Whiskers: range 10–90 % of each model's runs.
  • Table: Month · ECMWF average + chance above normal · BOM average + chance above normal. Yellow = clear lean (≥ 70 % or ≤ 30 %).

Limits

  • Monthly averages only – says nothing about single heatwaves or wind lulls.
  • Seasonal skill in Australia is modest outside strong El Niño / La Niña / Indian Ocean signals.
  • BOM's own published outlooks (bom.gov.au/climate/ahead) use ACCESS-S2 with BOM's own processing – numbers can differ a little.

medium.title: Region, next 15 days with range
medium.html:
How to read it

  • Narrow band = models agree, high confidence. Wide band = several outcomes possible – plan for both ends.
  • If IFS or AIFS sits at the edge of the band, it is an outlier run – trust the middle more.
  • Rain chance ≥ 70 % = likely wet day; ≤ 20 % = likely dry.
  • Confidence usually drops after day 5–7; days 10–15 are about the trend (warmer / cooler spell), not the exact number.

What you see

  • Title bar: code M1 · region picker (NSW / QLD / VIC / SA / TAS) · field picker (Temperature / Wind 100 m / Solar / Rain) · ⓘ (this card's "How to read it") · ▁ minimise. Edit mode adds A− / A+ (text size) and ✕ (remove). Region and field are remembered per panel, so a page can hold e.g. NSW temperature next to NSW wind.
  • Run pickers (W-017), after the title: run (default: latest) and vs (– none – or any earlier run on disk; default: the same time yesterday, else the run before). Remembered per panel. Runs here are ensemble runs (00z, once a day).
  • With a vs run: temperature / wind – the vs run's middle line dashed and its 10–90 % range as thin dashed edges; rain / solar – a hollow marker for the vs run's middle. Table Change column: high / low middle and rain chance vs that run (e.g. +1.5 / +0.8 · rain 20→70%). Big changes in yellow.
  • When an older run is picked, the IFS and AIFS lines show the runs of that same time if they are on disk.
  • Temperature / Wind 100 m chart:
    • Grey band = range 10–90 % of the 50 ensemble runs (8 in 10 runs fall inside).
    • Thick grey line = the middle run (median).
    • Blue line = IFS main model (single run). Purple line = AIFS AI model.
  • Rain / Solar chart: one bar per day = middle run's day total; whiskers = 10–90 % range; blue dot = IFS, purple diamond = AIFS.
  • Daily table: High and Low as "middle (low–high range)"; Rain = middle run mm + % chance of at least 1 mm; Wind = day average; Sun = day total kWh/m²; BOM = BOM's high / low, rain range and chance (BOM forecasts 7 days).
  • Temperature chart: BOM's daily high ▲ and low ▼ for its 7 days.

Limits

  • Days 8–15 have only 2 values a day (4 am / 4 pm), so peaks between can be missed in the chart; the table still uses the true max/min. Days 1–7 highs use 3-hour max windows every 6 hours – can read slightly low.
  • Ensemble "control" run (51st) not downloaded.
  • Raw model, no BOM correction yet.

short.title: Region, next 3 days
short.html:
How to read it

  • Dashed line far from the solid line = the forecast moved since that run; the Change column says how much.
  • Blue line inside a narrow band = confident. Blue line near the band's edge, or a wide band = the outcome could differ a lot – plan for both ends.
  • IFS and AIFS together: agree = more confidence.
  • ECMWF vs BOM: BOM's numbers are for the station and are adjusted by forecasters; ECMWF is a 25 km square average. A steady gap (e.g. ECMWF 2 °C cooler every day) is the model's usual bias; a gap on one day only means the two disagree about the weather.
  • Solar dips with cloud: dashed cloud line near 100 % at midday = weak solar.
  • 1 kWh/m² of daily sun ≈ a dull day; 7–8 kWh/m² ≈ a clear spring/summer day.

What you see

  • Title bar: code S1 · region picker (NSW / QLD / VIC / SA / TAS) · field picker (Temperature / Wind 100 m / Solar / Rain) · ⓘ (this card's "How to read it") · ▁ minimise. Edit mode adds A− / A+ (text size) and ✕ (remove). Region and field are remembered per panel, so a page can hold e.g. NSW temperature next to NSW wind.
  • Run pickers (W-017), after the title: run (default: latest) and vs (– none – or any earlier run on disk; default: the same time yesterday, else the run before). Remembered per panel.
  • With a vs run: the vs run's IFS line is drawn dashed in the same colour (temperature, wind, solar; rain as hollow bars) over the same 3 days; the table gets a Change column: high / low / rain vs that run (e.g. +2.1 / −0.4 / +6 mm). Big changes (±2 °C, ±5 mm) in yellow.
  • Chart (field from the title bar):
    • Temperature °C / Wind 100 m km/h:
      • blue line = IFS main model, every 3 hours (the best guess);
      • grey band = range 10–90 % of the 50 ensemble runs (8 in 10 runs inside), every 6 hours;
      • purple line = AIFS AI model, every 6 hours;
      • temperature only: BOM's forecast high ▲ and low ▼ for each day.
    • Solar W/m² – IFS, average over each 3 hours (drawn at the middle of the period) + ensemble 10–90 % band (6-hour averages); dashed line = IFS cloud cover %.
    • Rain – IFS mm in each 3 hours (bars).
  • Daily table (first 4 days):
    • High / Low °C (IFS), Rain (IFS day total mm) with the ensemble chance of ≥ 1 mm, Wind (day average km/h), Sun (day total kWh/m²);
    • BOM column: BOM's high / low, rain range and chance of rain (BOM's latest city forecast).
    • Grey italic rows = part days (the run starts or ends during that day).

Limits

  • Ensemble band is 6-hourly (the 3-hourly ensemble was not downloaded to save ~4 GB per refresh).
  • Ensemble may be one run older than IFS (we take the ensemble once a day, 00z).
  • Raw model, no BOM correction yet (W-008).
  • BOM forecast uses local time days (daylight saving) – matched to the same calendar date.
